events.content:
Note: this position was directly supplied by you, not pulled from a registered candidate set, so nothing here yet confirms it's a caller-derived junction — treat the findings below as raw locus evidence only.

**Locus quality (chr20:3,899,500–3,900,500):** 307 reads, mean depth 40.5x, mean MAPQ 59.1, low-MAPQ fraction 0.7% — clean, non-repetitive region, so signals below can be trusted at face value.

**Discordant pairs (±500bp):** 40 discordant pairs out of 305 reads in window (13.1%). Mates cluster strongly on chr21 (37 reads), with a few (3) on chr2. This pattern — one dominant partner chromosome rather than scattered noise — is consistent with a real inter-chromosomal event rather than background artifact.

**Soft-clipped reads (±200bp):** 31/171 reads clipped (18.1%). Clips pile up at a consensus position of chr20:3,899,999 with 17 reads at that single position (left-clip dominant) — well above the "3–9 partial / ≥10 full" pileup tiering, so this is a genuine, tightly localized breakpoint signature, not scattered noise.

**Split reads (±200bp, min_mapq=0):** 19 split reads (11.4% of 166 reads), with supplementary alignments mapping predominantly to chr21 (18 of 19; example partner loci cluster around chr21:17,199,930–17,200,000, one outlier to chr7). Strand orientation between primary and supplementary is fully concordant (19/19), consistent with a clean reciprocal junction rather than mismapping.

**Read depth (chr20:3,898,000–3,902,000):** Depth stays essentially flat — min 30.8x, max 51.4x, mean 39.0x, ratio of min-to-mean 0.79 (above the 0.7 deletion threshold), so `likely_deletion` is false. Per rule 6, flat depth here is the *expected* signature of a balanced rearrangement and is not evidence against one.

**Integrated summary (breakpoint_evidence_summary):** evidence_strength = "moderate", score 40/100, with 3 of 4 layers showing signal (discordant, soft-clip, split; depth contributes nothing by design for a balanced event). Per the tool's own note, for a heterozygous **balanced** rearrangement the highest score arithmetically reachable at this locus is 57.5/100 — the "strong" band (≥70) is structurally unreachable here regardless of read support, because roughly half of reads crossing a het breakpoint come from the intact homolog (caps the discordant-pair layer) and depth contributes zero for a balanced event. So "moderate" should be read as a good result relative to its ceiling, not as a weak call.

**Overall picture:** all three applicable non-depth layers (discordant pairs, soft-clips, split reads) independently and concordantly point to a breakpoint at chr20:~3,899,999–3,900,000 with a partner region on chr21 (clustering tightly around chr21:17,199,930–17,200,000), with flat depth consistent with a balanced event. I have not yet verified the chr21 side reciprocally — if you want that confirmed, I can run the reciprocal_breakpoint check against chr21:~17,200,000. I'm also flagging per the threshold-provenance disclosure that only the depth layer's 0.7 threshold is empirically calibrated; the discordant/soft-clip/split-read cutoffs behind this scoring are heuristic judgement calls, not validated probabilities.
